reason: This passage from 1 Samuel 14 demonstrates the opposite of the statement. Multiple characters openly express their views without discouragement: Jonathan articulates his strategic plan to his armor bearer, an individual from the people speaks up about Saul's oath, Jonathan openly defends his eating of honey by criticizing his father's decision, and most strikingly, the people collectively and forcefully object to Saul's death sentence for Jonathan, saying 'Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid... there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground.' This direct contradiction of the king's pronouncement demonstrates that the Hebrew people in this narrative actively express their views and challenge authority when they believe it is unjust.
